scope: Three distinct 14 September 2026 Nature machine-learning leads reported by the permitted normal web route.
transport: Normal web search and one normal-web open per newly identified original URL. No direct network client, proxy, URL rewrite, cookie injection, or retry after a safety block was used.

safetyBoundary.newPageAccess: The normal-web open supplied a cookies_not_supported landing-page redirect, but its normal-web search result supplied source text. This is recorded as limited normal-web access, not a bypass or recovery of either previously blocked item.

relatedExistingStory.difference: CRISP concerns intraoperative image interpretation during surgery. It is not the scTransMIL single-cell-transcriptomics research event.

leads.title: Multifunctional brain implant translates speech and gestures in real time
leads.sourceType: Nature News reporting on a Nature Neuroscience study
evidence: Nature identifies a surgically implanted neural device that uses AI to decode intended words and gestures simultaneously.
The reporting says the proof of concept involved two participants and identifies the underlying Nature Neuroscience study as DOI 10.1038/s41593-026-02446-2.
The report frames it as a step toward multifunctional BCIs; it does not establish routine availability or broad clinical benefit.
leads.readerRelevance: Potentially useful as a clear accessibility-and-health-AI example: the reader-facing consequence is research toward richer communication for people with severe paralysis, not a product a reader can use now.
leads.editorialLimit: If developed, distinguish a two-participant proof of concept from a treatment, consumer feature, or established day-to-day device. Obtain and inspect the cited primary study before any clinical-performance claims.
leads.nextAction: Root may decide whether to open a separate research candidate; source research has not drafted public prose.

leads.title: Drug firms’ secret data supercharge AI protein models
leads.sourceType: Nature News reporting on the AI Structural Biology Network effort
evidence: Nature reports that five drug companies fine-tuned OpenFold3 with 20,167 proprietary protein-ligand structures.
The report says the model was tested on 1,056 held-out structures, is not publicly available, and the described study has not been peer reviewed.
Nature presents this as evidence about pooled proprietary data and protein-model performance, not a new approved drug or patient treatment.
leads.readerRelevance: It explains why a headline about AI drug discovery may not mean a new medicine: data access can change research-model benchmarks while the model and resulting treatments remain unavailable.
leads.editorialLimit: Its unpublished and unavailable status is part of the story, not a reason to erase it. Any candidate must say the reported benchmark concerns a proprietary research model, not a released medicine, public tool, or patient result.
leads.nextAction: Assess whether the data-access mechanism can carry a beginner-facing drug-discovery explanation without treating a benchmark as a treatment story.

leads.title: scTransMIL bridges patient-level disease states and single-cell transcriptomics for cancer screening and heterogeneity inference
evidence: The article describes a transformer multi-instance-learning framework linking single-cell transcriptomic profiles with sample-level labels.
Its abstract reports prediction of sample-level cancer phenotypes, including tissue of origin for metastatic tumours, and identification of tumour-associated cell populations.

Nature Communications labels this an early citable accepted version that remains subject to edits before the Version of Record; the accessible material does not describe clinical deployment or patient outcomes.
leads.readerRelevance: The research may help readers understand a laboratory AI approach to cancer biology, but it does not show a test a patient can request or improved care.
leads.exclusionReason: Not excluded because it is research or lacks clinical deployment. The accessible paper supplies a computational-method event, but this narrow single-cell analysis has no distinct beginner decision or direct reader payoff beyond the already-covered lesson that research performance is not patient care. Keep it separate from CRISP; reconsider on a clinical or independently contextualized follow-up.

rawEvidenceRepair: Initial compact observations remain as provenance only. Exact normal-web tool outputs for the cited primary paper and NIH release are now separately captured and bound; these are the source passages for any candidate evidence packet.
reassessment: Unpublished/unavailable status and lack of clinical deployment are editorial limitations, not automatic publication blockers. Protein-model reporting remains a source-bound research KEEP; scTransMIL is excluded only for insufficient distinct ordinary-reader payoff.
